eulogies.opening: We lay down the hands that sutured our cuts when the power was dark.
eulogies.shift_line: {name} served {shifts_worked} shifts in the clinic, never turning away a neighbor who coughed from the ash.
eulogies.cooking_line: At supper, {name} gave away the extra bread portion to the children in bunk 4.
eulogies.relic_line: In their pocket was {keepsake}, worn smooth by ten thousand hours of quiet worry.
eulogies.closing: Let the granite wall hold their name so long as water flows clean through these pipes.

eulogies.opening: The boilers are quiet for an hour while we stand beside the grave.
eulogies.shift_line: {name} shoveled {shifts_worked} watches of anthracite into Boiler #2, keeping the frost from our beds.
eulogies.cooking_line: We remember how {name} could bake a loaf of rye right against the hot flue draft.
eulogies.relic_line: They left behind {keepsake}, stained with coal soot and oil.
eulogies.closing: The fire they kept alive is the warmth we still have. Rest in the cold earth.

eulogies.opening: The watch is relieved. The gate is secure.
eulogies.shift_line: {name} stood {shifts_worked} freezing watches at the surface intake, watching the whiteout storms.
eulogies.cooking_line: They drank the chicory tea cold so the stove wouldn't smoke during storm alerts.
eulogies.relic_line: Their hands held {keepsake} when the blizzard rattled the steel hatch.
eulogies.closing: No intruder breached our perimeter while they watched. We carry their watch forward.

eulogies.opening: The lathe is turned off, and the belt is slack.
eulogies.shift_line: {name} turned {shifts_worked} shifts on the foot-lathe, cutting brass valves from scrap copper.
eulogies.cooking_line: They always saved the marrow bones to boil grease for the shaft bearings.
eulogies.relic_line: They kept {keepsake} in their tool chest, calibrated to the thousandth of an inch.
eulogies.closing: Every wheel that turns in this bunker was trued by their eye. Peace to their bones.
